request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now has a "Watched due" figure that adds up the due-totals of the people the signed-in user watches, and shows 0.00 when they watch no one. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

It was a front-end-only change. The app already stores who each user watches and loads that list, so I didn't need to touch the server, the database or the audit file.

- **`features/header/header.ts`**: adds a `watchedDueTotal` input, shown in the "My figures" group as `data-testid="watched-due-total"`.
- **`features/people/people.ts`**: adds a `watchedDueTotal` value. It takes each watched person's due-total exactly as their row shows it (the cap applies), skips anyone whose total is n/a, and adds them up as-is. Unlike the sheet's main due-total, it doesn't drop the highest and lowest values. It updates straight away when the user watches or stops watching someone.
